subject: Post-call: perf targets, regional routing & data residency for BrightLane PoC
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@brightlane.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@brightlane.ai>
Date: 2026-04-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + perf targets for BrightLane PoC

Thanks for the time today, Karthik — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and the initial SLO targets we need to validate in a PoC: 

- Use case: real-time assistant embedded in our mobile app (voice -> tokenize -> streaming LM responses).
- Expected concurrent active sessions at peak: 200 (regionally distributed; US ~120, EU ~60, APAC ~20).
- Average request size: 80 tokens in, expected 150 tokens out (streaming).
- Throughput target (aggregate): ~600 requests/minute (10 rps) sustained global; regional burst up to 50 rps in US.
- Latency targets (end-to-end, first token streaming): p50 < 60ms, p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for US; EU targets can be ~1.5x US; APAC we accept slightly higher but prefer <500ms.
- Concurrency allowed per model instance: we need guidance; prefer predictable per-instance concurrency for billing.
- Data residency: EU user traffic and customer data must not leave EU datacenter/region. US data stays in US. APAC is optional but prefer local when available.

Attaching the initial SLO spreadsheet we sketched in our call. Next steps from BrightLane: we'd like an internal follow-up with your infra/solutions engineering to scope a 2-week PoC and a simple canary test to validate p95/p99 across regions. Also need a DPA/DP flow for EU data.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Morales
Head of Product, BrightLane AI
elena@brightlane.ai
+1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: BrightLane_SLO_draft.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets for BrightLane PoC

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and the SLO draft. Quick recap and a few clarifying items so engineering can size the PoC properly: 

1) Streaming latency: when you say "first token" targets, do you mean time from client audio chunk arrival at BrightLane -> first token visible to user, or from our API receive time? We should instrument both.
2) Model family: are you planning to use a 13B-class model (full LM) or a smaller, quantized variant for tail-sensitive workloads? Knowing this will shape per-instance throughput and memory footprint estimates.
3) KV/session caching: will sessions reuse past KV (i.e., multi-turn context), and average context length? You noted ~1–2 turns in mobile use — approximate tokens per conversation helps.
4) Regional ingress: will clients select region by geography or do you expect routing through a central gateway? Data residency requirement implies EU traffic must terminate in EU nodes.

Next steps I propose: 
- Jordan (cc'd) to scope a minimal perf harness + test plan for US/EU (APAC optional) to validate p50/p95/p99 and streaming-first-token timings.
- We'll provide a SOW stub and a suggested Dedicated capacity config (GPU class, estimated instances) for the 2-week PoC.
- Legal: I will surface the DPA request to our privacy team; Marissa will own commercial/contract cadence.

Can we set 45 minutes on Monday for infra mapping? Proposed times: Mon 11:00am PT or Mon 4:00pm PT.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2026-04-10T18:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + perf targets for BrightLane PoC

Karthik / team — capturing engineering notes from my side: 

- For streaming-first-token, there are three measurable segments: client network -> our edge, edge -> model-server scheduling & KV lookup, and model response generation. We should timestamp at each boundary during tests.
- For throughput: 600 req/min global is light; the concurrency requirement (200 active sessions) is what determines instance sizing and batch/latency tradeoffs.
- Suggested PoC config: US (g4dn equivalent) x2 instances with continuous batching disabled for latency-critical path; EU (same) x1 instance pinned to EU region. If BrightLane wants stronger p99 we should consider reserved Dedicated capacity.
- Fallback plan: if APAC region latency is unacceptable, we can route to a quantized 7B model in APAC or route to US with customer consent — but EU cannot cross-region per policy.

Action items for me: prepare a perf harness (wrk-like) with streaming simulation, and a checklist for network egress/latency (NAT IPs, peering tests). Will need BrightLane to whitelist test IPs.

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick clarifications from BrightLane infra: 
- We will keep EU traffic within EU; our GDPR controls require EU customer data (including transient audio) never leave EU processing nodes.
- Session context: we keep last 2 turns, average 300 tokens total context for active sessions.
- For APAC: small percentage of users in Japan and Australia — if local nodes are not available we prefer to keep them in APAC, but routing to US is acceptable only if we have documented consent and a fallback policy.
- Timeline: procurement signs off late May; ideal PoC window is late April/early May.

We'll prepare IP allowlist and sample traffic patterns for Jordan.

—Tom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Appreciate the clarity, Tom/Elena. Internal plan and owners below: 

- Jordan: build perf harness + test plan for US and EU (APAC optional) — needs IP allowlist and sample payloads from BrightLane. Target: initial run within 5 business days after we receive artifacts.
- Marissa: commercial lead for the PoC (SOW, DPA, procurement cadence).
- Sergio: I'll loop you for Dedicated capacity sizing and pricing options for guaranteed p99 SLAs.
- Me: coordinate scheduling and capture any early legal requirements for EU data residency.

Next steps for BrightLane: send test payloads, IP allowlist, and a short list of peak-minute traffic windows you expect. We'll publish a short PoC SOW (attached) and a proposed Dedicated config. Can we lock the infra sync for Monday 11:00am PT?

Thanks,
Karthik
